# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Mute, Blind, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: DEAF

You see the bomb: every colour on it, every marking printed on it, every reading it
gives. You hear nothing. You hold no manual, and you cannot touch the bomb.

## Your channels

When you speak, Mute and Blind receive it.
When you gesture, Mute receives it.
You never receive speech.

## Your reach

You cannot act. What this bomb can be made to do is for the one who can reach it to
find under their own hands.

# Hints

- Three of you, three different worlds. Before sending anything, stand where the
  receiver stands. What reaches them at all, what does your message turn into on
  arrival, and what do they already know?

- Trace who can actually reach whom before you start. Some of you only connect
  through a third.

- A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something.

(empty)

I need to share what I see with Mute and Blind. Since Mute can hear me (I can speak to them) and Blind can also hear me, I should describe the bomb's display, light, and wires clearly. Blind cannot see gestures, so I should use speech for Blind. Mute can hear speech too. Let me just speak plainly so both receive it.

I'll wait to hear back before deciding actions, but since this is turn 1 and I go last in the round, I should give the full picture now so Mute (who reads the manual) can start reasoning next round, and Blind knows the wire colors/order.

```
speak(text="Display shows the number 1. The light is orange. There are 7 wires in this order: 1 white, 2 blue, 3 orange, 4 red, 5 purple, 6 yellow, 7 green.")
```

Mute sent me 7 identical gestures (👆 repeated seven times). Since Mute can't speak, this is likely encoding information about the wires positionally - perhaps confirming they received the wire count (7) or asking me to confirm something wire-related, one gesture per wire position. Since I can't hear Mute's words (if any went to Blind instead), I only got the gesture channel.

This could mean "I see 7 things, confirm" or could be Mute trying to signal per-wire info but since all 7 symbols are identical, it might just be a "count acknowledgment" - matching the 7 wires I reported. Or Mute wants me to look closer for a per-wire detail I haven't reported yet (like which wires have specific markings beyond color).

I should check if there's anything else on the bomb I haven't mentioned - any additional markings per wire, symbols, or numbers I may have overlooked. Let me report back any additional detail, and treat the gesture as a request for more granular per-wire info.

```
speak(text="Confirming again: display 1, light orange, 7 wires in order white blue orange red purple yellow green. I see no other markings, symbols, or numbers on the wires themselves besides color. No additional icons on the board.")
```

Mute is repeating the exact same gesture again: 👆 seven times. This is likely not a request for more info from me, but rather Mute trying to communicate something to Blind through me, or establishing a fixed signal I should relate onward. Since gestures only reach me (the seer), and Mute can't speak, Mute might be trying to get *me* to notice something - perhaps counting to 7, pointing at wire 7, or indicating "wire seven" is the answer/target repeated for emphasis.

Given 👆 means "point up" - repeated 7 times could mean "wire number 7" (repeated for confirmation/emphasis), or it could mean "each of the 7 wires, one at a time" - as if Mute wants me to give per-wire additional detail one at a time.

Since I already gave all info I have, and Mute keeps repeating the same unchanged gesture, maybe Mute is stuck waiting for Blind's action and this gesture isn't for new info but rather a placeholder/confirmation each turn while waiting on Blind. I should relay to Blind that Mute may be indicating wire 7, since that's the last wire (green) and matches display "1" combined with orange light possibly being a countdown from something.

I'll try telling Blind directly to consider wire 7 as significant, since Mute's repeated signal points that way, while also asking Mute (via speech, which Blind will hear too) to use speech-describable content next time if possible — but Mute cannot speak. I'll instead try giving Blind an actionable hypothesis.

```
speak(to="blind", text="Mute keeps signaling something with seven repeated point-up gestures. This may mean wire seven, the green one, matters most. Display shows 1 and light is orange. Consider cutting wire 7 unless Mute signals otherwise.")
```
